subject: arctic fox
title: An Arctic Fox Walked 2,175 Miles From Norway to Canada

scenes.text: A fox walked from Norway to Canada. Nobody believed it.
A young female arctic fox left Svalbard on March twenty-sixth, twenty eighteen, wearing a GPS tag.
Seventy-six days later she reached Ellesmere Island in Canada. That's more than 2,175 miles.
She crossed sea ice and Greenland, and in one day covered about 96 miles, the fastest ever recorded for her species.
The research team said they didn't think it was true.
Norway to Canada, on foot, in seventy-six days.

description:
A young arctic fox walked from Svalbard, Norway, to Ellesmere Island, Canada, in 76 days.
She covered more than 2,175 miles, including one day of about 96 miles, a record for her species.
What is the longest walk you have ever done? Comment below.
first_comment: The scientists doubted the data at first. Would you have? Which animal journey amazes you most?
